chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Mutt's bragging; Kid Thomas and Keppard compared
summary: Joe says Mutt boasted constantly, then Barry and Joe compare Kid Thomas, Freddie Keppard and Kid Rena.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What did Mutt think of his own playing? Did he ever talk about his own playing?
Oh, Mutt thought he was the greatest thing in the world, if you listened to him. He was the braggin'est you ever seen in your life! One of these
typical New Orleans like Kid Thomas or one of them guys, pretend to know it all.
I've seen in so many Jazz books that Kid Thomas is the nearest thing to Freddie Keppard. Now, you've heard them both play. Who would you say...
[CHUCKLES] Kid Thomas... I never heard... Maybe he was capable of doing it. But I never seen that power that Freddie had.
See, me, I don't know how they come about that. I know Kid Thomas' playing and I know Freddie's playing.
Oh, you hear so many different things about... Kid Rena was another helluva trumpet player when I was little.

But as for Kid Thomas being the nearest thing to Keppard... I just wanted to see what you thought. To me there's no comparison at all. One is a first-class musician, the other is sort of...well, you know...
